claim: Irrigation induces a significant change in the soil microbiome.
source: Irrigation induces a significant change in the soil microbiome
evidence: The claim is supported by 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing data showing changes in bacterial populations between irrigated and non-irrigated sites, as presented in Figure 1.

claim: 26 bacterial orders were determined to significantly differ across one or more sampling sites using voom with a false discovery rate of 0.05.
source: In total, changes were observed for 26 bacterial orders (Figure 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis (voom with FDR 0.05) and visualized in Figure 1A showing the 26 bacterial orders with significant differences.

claim: Significant population changes were observed for eight bacterial orders between the irrigated (A2) and nonirrigated (B2) sites.
source: Significant population changes (FDR < 0.05) were also observed for eight bacterial orders between the irrigated (A2) and nonirrigated (B2) sites (Figure 1B and C)
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis with FDR < 0.05 and presented in Figure 1B and C.

claim: A larger proportion of Pseudomonadales bacteria was found in the irrigated site compared to the non-irrigated site.
source: Significant population changes (FDR < 0.05) were also observed for eight bacterial orders between the irrigated (A2) and nonirrigated (B2) sites (Figure 1B and C), including a larger proportion of Pseudomonadales bacteria in the irrigated site.
evidence: The claim is supported by amplicon sequencing data showing increased Pseudomonadales in irrigated conditions, as shown in Figure 1C.

claim: No significant changes were observed between pre-planting sites A1 and B1.
source: In contrast, despite the potential for microbial heterogeneity across the fertilized field prior to planting, no significant changes were observed between pre-planting sites A1 and B1.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of amplicon sequencing data comparing pre-planting sites.

claim: 240 individual Pseudomonas strains were isolated from pre- and post-irrigation field sites.
source: To investigate the diversity of the fluorescent pseudomonad population, we isolated 240 individual Pseudomonas strains from our pre- and post-irrigation field sites (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is a direct statement of the experimental procedure performed.

claim: 79% of Pseudomonas isolates were outcompeted by S. scabies in the cross-streak assay.
source: On-plate suppression of S. scabies was a surprisingly rare trait, with 79% of Pseudomonas isolates outcompeted by S. scabies in this assay.
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic screening data from cross-streak assays.

claim: 69 isolates were selected for whole-genome sequencing.
source: To determine whether this suppressive activity correlated with specific genetic loci, 69 isolates were selected for whole-genome sequencing
evidence: The claim is a direct statement of the experimental procedure performed.

claim: The sequenced strain collection spans much of the characterized global phylogenetic diversity and contains representatives of at least five of the eight P. fluorescens phylogenomic groups.
source: Our sequenced strain collection spans much of this characterized global phylogenetic diversity and contains representatives of at least five of the eight P. fluorescens phylogenomic groups (Garrido-Sanz et al., 2016), as well as strains belonging to the Pseudomonas putida and Pseudomonas syringae groups (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis comparing the sequenced strains to reference strains from defined phylogenomic groups, as shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: 787 gene clusters were identified that could be subdivided into 61 gene cluster families.
source: In total, 787 gene clusters were identified that could be subdivided into 61 gene cluster families (Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis of the sequenced genomes using antiSMASH and manual annotation.

claim: The top 10 positively correlating genotypes and phenotypes with S. scabies inhibition comprised four BGC families (Pep1, CLP, Pep2, and HCN), four accessory genome loci (chitinase ChiC, protease AprA, chitinase class 1, and the Pga operon), and two phenotypes (motility and secreted protease production).
source: The top 10 positively correlating genotypes and phenotypes (Figure 3) comprised four BGC families (Pep1, CLP, Pep2, and HCN) (Appendix 1—figure 2), four accessory genome loci (chitinase ChiC, protease AprA, chitinase class 1, and the Pga operon), and two phenotypes (motility and secreted protease production).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pearson correlation analysis between genotypes/phenotypes and S. scabies inhibition, as shown in Figure 3.

claim: The production of HCN and/or CLPs by Pseudomonas strains has been previously associated with the suppression of various plant pathogens including fungi and oomycetes.
source: The production of HCN and/or CLPs by Pseudomonas strains has been previously associated with the suppression of various plant pathogens including fungi (Michelsen et al., 2015; Zachow et al., 2015) and oomycetes (Hultberg et al., 2010; Hunziker et al., 2015), and can also contribute to insect killing (Flury et al., 2017; Jang et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: HCN and CLPs have not been linked to the suppression of bacteria prior to this study.
source: The production of HCN and/or CLPs by Pseudomonas strains has been previously associated with the suppression of various plant pathogens including fungi (Michelsen et al., 2015; Zachow et al., 2015) and oomycetes (Hultberg et al., 2010; Hunziker et al., 2015), and can also contribute to insect killing (Flury et al., 2017; Jang et al., 2013), but have not been linked to the suppression of bacteria.
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of citations linking HCN/CLPs to bacterial suppression in the literature review.

claim: P. fluorescens strains from a single field have the collective capacity to make viscosin, a viscosin isomer, tensin, anikasin, putisolvin II, syringafactin A, and cichofactin.
source: These data showed that P. fluorescens strains from a single field have the collective capacity to make viscosin (m/z 1126.69, identical retention time to a viscosin standard) (de Bruijn et al., 2007), a viscosin isomer (m/z 1126.69, different retention time to viscosin standard) (Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2), as well as compounds with BGCs, exact masses, and MS/MS fragmentation consistent with tensin (m/z 1409.85, Figure 4—figure supplement 3; Nielsen et al., 2000), anikasin (m/z 1354.81, Figure 4—figure supplement 4; Götze et al., 2017), and putisolvin II (m/z 1394.85, Figure 4—figure supplement 5; Kuiper et al., 2004). In addition, an array of related metabolites were observed that differed by 14 or 28 Da, which is characteristic of different lipid chain lengths. This analysis also proved that the linear lipopeptides syringafactin A (m/z 1082.74) and cichofactin (m/z 555.38, [M + 2 H]2+) were made by strains harboring BGCs predicted to make these phytotoxins (Götze et al., 2019; Pauwelyn et al., 2013; Figure 4—figure supplements 6 and 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by LC-MS/MS analysis identifying these compounds based on mass, retention time, and MS/MS fragmentation patterns, as shown in Figure 4 and supplementary figures.

claim: The Ps682 ∆visc strain was unable to make the viscosin-like molecule (m/z 1126.69).
source: The resulting Ps682 ∆visc strain was unable to make the viscosin-like molecule (m/z 1126.69, Figure 5B)
evidence: The claim is supported by LC-MS analysis comparing wild-type and mutant strains, as shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The Ps682 ∆visc strain was unable to undergo swarming motility.
source: The resulting Ps682 ∆visc strain was unable to make the viscosin-like molecule (m/z 1126.69, Figure 5B) or to undergo swarming motility (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by motility assays comparing wild-type and mutant strains, as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Possession of a CLP BGC was the genotype that most strongly correlated with motility (ρ = 0.65).
source: This is in agreement with earlier work on the role of viscosin in the motility of P. fluorescens SBW25 (Alsohim et al., 2014) and the observation that possession of a CLP BGC was the genotype that most strongly correlated with motility (ρ = 0.65, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pearson correlation analysis as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A cross-streak assay with S. scabies revealed an active role for the viscosin-like CLP in on-plate S. scabies inhibition.
source: A cross-streak assay with S. scabies revealed an active role for this CLP in on-plate S. scabies inhibition (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by cross-streak assays comparing wild-type and mutant strains, as shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Wild-type Ps682 appeared to specifically colonize the S. scabies streak, whereas Ps682 ∆visc was unable to restrict S. scabies growth.
source: Wild-type (WT) Ps682 appeared to specifically colonize the S. scabies streak, whereas Ps682 ∆visc was unable to restrict S. scabies growth.
evidence: The claim is supported by visual observation of cross-streak assays shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Bioluminescence imaging clearly showed viscosin-dependent Pseudomonas colonization of the Streptomyces streaks.
source: To distinguish between these possible inhibition modes, a constitutively expressed lux operon was integrated into the chromosomal att::Tn7 site (K.-H. Choi et al., 2005) of Ps682 to visualize this interaction by bioluminescence. This clearly showed viscosin-dependent Pseudomonas colonization of the Streptomyces streaks (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioluminescence imaging of lux-tagged strains in cross-streak assays, as shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The Ps682 CLP has an identical amino acid composition to viscosin (3-hydroxydecanoic acid-Leu1-Glu2-Thr3-Val4-Leu5-Ser6-Leu7-Ser8-Ile9).
source: NMR analysis revealed that the molecule has an identical amino acid composition to viscosin (3-hydroxydecanoic acid-Leu1-Glu2-Thr3-Val4-Leu5-Ser6-Leu7-Ser8-Ile9, Figure 5B)
evidence: The claim is supported by NMR spectroscopy data (1H, 13C, COSY, HSQC, TOCSY, HMBC) as shown in Figure 5—figure supplements 3–13.

claim: The LC retention time of the Ps682 CLP is different to viscosin, but is almost identical to WLIP.
source: The LC retention time of this CLP is different to viscosin, but is almost identical to WLIP (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: The claim is supported by LC-MS retention time comparison as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The Ps682 CLP was named viscosin I (for viscosin Isomer) because its absolute configuration could not be conclusively confirmed.
source: Therefore, we could not conclusively confirm the absolute configuration of the Ps682 CLP and thus named it viscosin I (for viscosin Isomer).
evidence: The claim is based on the inability to definitively determine stereochemistry from NMR data, leading to a naming decision.

claim: Purified viscosin I directly inhibited S. scabies growth with a minimum inhibitory concentration of approximately 20 µg/mL.
source: A disk diffusion assay of purified viscosin I with S. scabies (Figure 5C) demonstrated that it directly inhibited S. scabies growth with a minimum inhibitory concentration of approximately 20 µg/mL.
evidence: The claim is supported by disk diffusion assay data as shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The inhibition of S. scabies by viscosin I is temporary and growth partially resumes after several days.
source: Long-term growth of S. scabies in the presence of viscosin I (Figure 5—figure supplement 14) indicated that the inhibition of S. scabies is temporary and growth partially resumes after several days.
evidence: The claim is supported by time-course disk diffusion assay data as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 14.

claim: Viscosin I functions by inhibiting the growth rate of S. scabies.
source: These data show that in addition to its role as a surfactant viscosin I functions by inhibiting the growth rate of S. scabies, consistent with the on-plate data for Ps682 ∆visc.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from disk diffusion assay data and genetic deletion experiments.

claim: 17 of the 19 strains containing HCN gene clusters were inhibitory towards S. scabies.
source: Pan-genome analysis showed that HCN production was predicted for a significant number of suppressive strains (ρ = 0.47, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), where 17 of the 19 strains containing HCN gene clusters were inhibitory towards S. scabies (Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis and phenotypic data as shown in Figures 2 and 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nearly every strain with the hcnABC gene cluster produced HCN (18 out of 19).
source: We confirmed that nearly every strain with the hcnABC gene cluster produced HCN (18 out of 19) using the Feigl–Anger colorimetric detection reagent (Feigl and Anger, 1966; Supplementary file 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by colorimetric assay data using the Feigl–Anger reagent.

claim: HCN production strongly correlated with S. scabies inhibition (ρ = 0.52) across the original collection of 240 Pseudomonas strains.
source: This wider analysis showed that HCN production strongly correlated with S. scabies inhibition (ρ = 0.52, Figure 6—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by Pearson correlation analysis as shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: HCN inhibits S. scabies growth and development across the entire plate.
source: A comparison of WT, single, and double mutants showed that HCN inhibits S. scabies growth and development across the entire plate
evidence: The claim is supported by cross-streak assays comparing Ps619 wild-type and mutant strains, as shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Tensin is important for Pseudomonas motility and helps the Pseudomonas to grow competitively at the cross-streak interface.
source: A comparison of WT, single, and double mutants showed that HCN inhibits S. scabies growth and development across the entire plate, while tensin is important for Pseudomonas motility and helps the Pseudomonas to grow competitively at the cross-streak interface.
evidence: The claim is supported by cross-streak assays comparing Ps619 wild-type and mutant strains, as shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The suppressive effect of HCN and tensin is additive.
source: Furthermore, this suppressive effect is additive: the Ps619 Δhcn and Δten single mutants both retained some inhibitory activity towards S. scabies, whereas the Ps619 ΔhcnΔten double mutant could not inhibit S. scabies.
evidence: The claim is supported by cross-streak assays comparing single and double mutants, as shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The tensin-like CLP induces a developmental defect in S. scabies that is independent of Pseudomonas motility.
source: Notably, Ps619 Δhcn was able to induce a developmental defect in S. scabies at the microbial interface that was not present in Ps619 Δten or Ps619 ΔhcnΔten, showing that the tensin-like CLP induces a developmental defect in S. scabies that is independent of Pseudomonas motility
evidence: The claim is supported by cross-streak assays in drier conditions comparing mutant strains, as shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: At areas distant from the bacterial interaction, S. scabies grew more vigorously when cultured with Δhcn strains, consistent with the volatility of HCN enabling a long-range inhibitory effect.
source: This analysis also clearly showed that at areas distant from the bacterial interaction S. scabies grew more vigorously when cultured with Δhcn strains, consistent with the volatility of HCN enabling a long-range inhibitory effect.
evidence: The claim is supported by cross-streak assays comparing mutant strains, as shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Only Ps619 strains producing HCN inhibited S. scabies growth and development when separated by a barrier.
source: A similar volatile effect was seen when Ps619 strains were separated from S. scabies by a barrier, where only those strains producing HCN inhibited growth and development (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by split plate assays as shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Wild-type Ps619 inhibited S. scabies development, which appears as a mixture of deformed aerial hyphae and vegetative growth reminiscent of a 'bald' phenotype.
source: WT Ps619 was able to colonize the S. scabies streak, meaning that the interfacial region imaged was further from the cross-streak intersection than all other co-cultures (Figure 6C). Here, Ps619 inhibited S. scabies development, which appears as a mixture of deformed aerial hyphae and vegetative growth reminiscent of a 'bald' phenotype (Tschowri et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-SEM imaging of the microbial interface as shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Both the Ps619 Δhcn and Δten mutants induced a similar partially bald phenotype in S. scabies.
source: Cryo-SEM indicated that both the Ps619 Δhcn and Δten mutants induced a similar partially bald phenotype in S. scabies
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-SEM imaging of the microbial interface as shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The Ps619 ΔhcnΔten double mutant was unable to trigger the same developmental defect as S. scabies could develop aerial mycelia close to the microbial interface.
source: Cryo-SEM indicated that both the Ps619 Δhcn and Δten mutants induced a similar partially bald phenotype in S. scabies, but the ΔhcnΔten double mutant was unable to trigger the same developmental defect as S. scabies could develop aerial mycelia close to the microbial interface (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-SEM imaging of the microbial interface as shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Ps619 conferred significant protection against potato scab, where disease severity was reduced to levels similar to uninfected control plants.
source: Ps619 conferred significant protection against potato scab, where disease severity was reduced to levels similar to uninfected control plants (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta biocontrol experiments as shown in Figure 7.

claim: The suppressive ability of Ps619 was lost for Ps619 Δten and Ps619 ΔhcnΔten, resulting in disease severity similar to scab-infected tubers.
source: This suppressive ability was lost for Ps619 Δten and Ps619 ΔhcnΔten, resulting in disease severity similar to scab-infected tubers.
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta biocontrol experiments as shown in Figure 7.

claim: Ps619 Δhcn was just as effective as WT Ps619 at suppressing potato scab.
source: In contrast, Ps619 Δhcn was just as effective as WT Ps619 at suppressing potato scab, which differed from the on-plate results for HCN.
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta biocontrol experiments as shown in Figure 7.

claim: The significance of the in planta biocontrol results was supported by an independent experiment where equivalent results were obtained for each strain.
source: The significance of these results was supported by an independent in planta biocontrol experiment, where equivalent results were obtained for each strain (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by a replicate in planta biocontrol experiment as shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tensin plays an important role in the biocontrol of potato scab.
source: This result indicates that tensin plays an important role in the biocontrol of potato scab.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from in planta biocontrol experiments showing loss of activity in Δten mutants.

claim: Potato scab assays showed no significant antagonistic activity for Ps682 against S. scabies infection.
source: In contrast to its on-plate suppressive activity, potato scab assays showed no significant antagonistic activity for Ps682 against S. scabies infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta biocontrol experiments as shown in Figure 7.

claim: Neither HCN nor tensin were required for Ps619 inhibition of either G. graminis or P. infestans.
source: Surprisingly, neither HCN or tensin were required for Ps619 inhibition of either G. graminis or P. infestans (Appendix 2—figure 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by pathogen inhibition assays with mutant strains as shown in Appendix 2—figure 1.

claim: Inactivation of the viscosin I pathway in Ps682 abolished activity towards both G. graminis and P. infestans.
source: In contrast, inactivation of the viscosin I pathway in Ps682 abolished activity towards both pathogens (Appendix 2—figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathogen inhibition assays with mutant strains as shown in Appendix 2—figure 1D.

claim: A greater number of strongly suppressive strains (inhibition score ≥2) were isolated from nonirrigated sites (7/60 strains) than from irrigated sites (1/60 strains).
source: However, a greater number of strongly suppressive strains (inhibition score ≥2) were isolated from nonirrigated sites (7/60 strains) than from irrigated sites (1/60 strains).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic screening data from the second sampling event.

claim: A similar pattern was observed for strongly motile (score ≥2) strains (six nonirrigated versus two irrigated).
source: A similar pattern was observed for strongly motile (score ≥2) strains (six nonirrigated versus two irrigated).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic screening data from the second sampling event.

claim: 5/18 unirrigated strains contained CLP BGCs versus 0/16 irrigated strains.
source: Analysis of the BGCs in our sequenced strains revealed a similar result, where 5/18 unirrigated strains contained CLP BGCs versus 0/16 irrigated strains.
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic analysis of sequenced strains from the first sampling event.

claim: A negative correlation was observed between irrigation and S. scabies suppression on the plant roots, but not in the surrounding soil.
source: A negative correlation was observed between irrigation and S. scabies suppression on the plant roots, but not in the surrounding soil.
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic screening data from the second sampling event as shown in Figure 8A.

claim: A substantially greater proportion of suppressive isolates were associated with roots than with the surrounding soil in unirrigated samples.
source: This appeared to be driven primarily by differences in the unirrigated samples, where a substantially greater proportion of suppressive isolates were associated with roots than with the surrounding soil.
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic screening data from the second sampling event as shown in Figure 8A.

claim: A strong positive correlation was observed between motility and root association for unirrigated samples, while the reverse was true for irrigated plants.
source: We observed a strong positive correlation between motility and root association for unirrigated samples, while the reverse was true for irrigated plants (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic screening data from the second sampling event as shown in Figure 8A.

claim: In dry plants, the motile population was almost entirely associated with roots, while in irrigated plants a comparable proportion of motile bacteria were found in the soil and roots.
source: This effect of irrigation on the distribution of motile bacteria was striking – in dry plants, the motile population was almost entirely associated with roots, while in irrigated plants a comparable proportion of motile bacteria were found in the soil and roots (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic screening data from the second sampling event as shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The P. fluorescens population in a single field is highly complex, heterogeneous, and dynamic.
source: This population-level approach shows that the P. fluorescens population in a single field is highly complex, heterogeneous, and dynamic (Figures 2, 3 and 8)
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic, genomic, and phenotypic analysis across multiple sampling events as shown in Figures 2, 3, and 8.

claim: The overall genotypic diversity of the P. fluorescens population in a single field is similar to the global diversity of P. fluorescens.
source: This population-level approach shows that the P. fluorescens population in a single field is highly complex, heterogeneous, and dynamic (Figures 2, 3 and 8), where the overall genotypic diversity is similar to the global diversity of P. fluorescens (Garrido-Sanz et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis comparing field isolates to global reference strains, as shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: HCN and a tensin-like CLP produced by Ps619 arrest the formation of streptomycete aerial hyphae and subsequent sporulation.
source: Co-culture assays and cryo-SEM imaging (Figure 6) showed that HCN and a tensin-like CLP produced by Ps619 arrest the formation of streptomycete aerial hyphae and subsequent sporulation
evidence: The claim is supported by cross-streak assays and cryo-SEM imaging as shown in Figure 6.

claim: HCN and a tensin-like CLP provide the pseudomonad with a competitive advantage at the microbial interface.
source: Co-culture assays and cryo-SEM imaging (Figure 6) showed that HCN and a tensin-like CLP produced by Ps619 arrest the formation of streptomycete aerial hyphae and subsequent sporulation, providing the pseudomonad with a competitive advantage at the microbial interface.
evidence: The claim is supported by cross-streak assays and cryo-SEM imaging as shown in Figure 6.

claim: CLP production was a key determinant of potato scab suppression by Ps619 in planta.
source: In planta experiments confirmed that Ps619 could suppress potato scab and that CLP production was a key determinant of this inhibitory effect (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta biocontrol experiments with mutant strains as shown in Figure 7.

claim: HCN production was not a requirement for potato scab suppression by Ps619.
source: In contrast, HCN production was not a requirement for potato scab suppression by Ps619.
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta biocontrol experiments showing that Ps619 Δhcn retained suppressive activity as shown in Figure 7.

claim: Irrigation enables nonsuppressive Pseudomonas spp. with low motility to be transported to plant roots more effectively.
source: One possible reason for this discrepancy is that irrigation enables nonsuppressive Pseudomonas spp. with low motility to be transported to plant roots more effectively.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis proposed to explain the observation that irrigation decreases the proportion of suppressive pseudomonads on roots.

claim: Recruitment of nonsuppressive pseudomonads to the rhizosphere may benefit the plant in other ways, such as immune system priming or modulation of auxin biosynthesis.
source: Recruitment of nonsuppressive pseudomonads to the rhizosphere may benefit the plant in other ways, such as immune system priming (Bakker et al., 2007; Teixeira et al., 2021) or modulation of auxin biosynthesis.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis supported by citations to previous studies on plant-microbe interactions.

claim: Auxin biosynthesis was linked to plant growth promotion and induced systemic resistance by P. fluorescens SS101.
source: For example, Cheng et al., 2017 showed that auxin biosynthesis was linked to plant growth promotion and induced systemic resistance by P. fluorescens SS101.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Changes in the overall relative abundance of soil Pseudomonas over Streptomyces resulting from irrigation may override the observed shift towards less-suppressive Pseudomonas genotypes.
source: An alternative hypothesis is that changes in the overall relative abundance of soil Pseudomonas over Streptomyces resulting from irrigation may override the observed shift towards less-suppressive Pseudomonas genotypes.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis proposed to explain the effectiveness of irrigation despite decreased suppressive genotypes.

claim: Drought-induced enrichment for commensal Streptomyces and depletion of Proteobacteria in sorghum and rice plants have been shown to be reversed by irrigation.
source: In support of this, drought-induced enrichment for commensal Streptomyces and depletion of Proteobacteria in sorghum and rice plants have been shown to be reversed by irrigation (Santos-Medellín et al., 2021; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Irrigation may reduce the relative fitness of S. scabies versus Pseudomonas spp., while the microbiome of irrigated roots simultaneously becomes less optimal for disease suppression.
source: In this model, irrigation may reduce the relative fitness of S. scabies versus Pseudomonas spp., while the microbiome of irrigated roots simultaneously becomes less optimal for disease suppression.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model to explain the complex relationship between irrigation, microbiome composition, and disease suppression.

claim: Ps619 is highly effective at inhibiting potato scab, yet Ps619-like strains are naturally less abundant in irrigated conditions.
source: Our data show that Ps619 is highly effective at inhibiting potato scab, yet Ps619-like strains are naturally less abundant in irrigated conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta biocontrol experiments and strain isolation data from irrigated vs. non-irrigated sites.

claim: Possible future efforts to control potato scab could combine irrigation with pretreatment with effective biocontrol strains, like Ps619, to ensure tubers are colonized by a significant proportion of biocontrol strains.
source: Therefore, possible future efforts to control potato scab could combine irrigation with pretreatment with effective biocontrol strains, like Ps619, to ensure tubers are colonized by a significant proportion of biocontrol strains.
evidence: The claim is a proposed application based on the findings of the study.

claim: Such a strategy could reduce the quantity of water required for effective scab suppression.
source: Such a strategy could reduce the quantity of water required for effective scab suppression.
evidence: The claim is a speculative prediction about the potential benefits of the proposed biocontrol strategy.

claim: Interactions between fluorescent pseudomonads and the wider microbiome may also have a key role in potato scab suppression.
source: While our study was focused on fluorescent pseudomonads, interactions between these bacteria and the wider microbiome (Figure 1) may also have a key role in potato scab suppression.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on the observation of microbiome changes shown in Figure 1.

claim: The most significant changes in bacterial populations were observed between January and May regardless of irrigation.
source: In total, changes were observed for 26 bacterial orders (Figure 1A), with the most significant changes observed between January and May regardless of irrigation.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of amplicon sequencing data as shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Changes in bacterial populations between January and May partially reflect an increase in bacterial orders that have previously been associated with the potato root microbiome, including Rhizobiales, Sphingomonadales, and Flavobacteriales.
source: This partially reflects an increase in bacterial orders that have previously been associated with the potato root microbiome (Pfeiffer et al., 2017; Weinert et al., 2011), including Rhizobiales, Sphingomonadales, and Flavobacteriales.
evidence: The claim is supported by amplicon sequencing data and citations to previous studies on the potato root microbiome.

claim: A significant increase in the abundance of Pseudomonas taxa has been observed for irrigated fields, correlating with reduced levels of potato scab.
source: A significant increase in the abundance of Pseudomonas taxa has been observed for irrigated fields, correlating with reduced levels of potato scab (Elphinstone et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Naturally scab-suppressive soils have been shown to contain a greater proportion of Pseudomonas when compared to scab-conducive soils.
source: Naturally scab-suppressive soils have also been shown to contain a greater proportion of Pseudomonas when compared to scab-conducive soils (Meng et al., 2012; Rosenzweig et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Phenazine production by P. fluorescens can contribute to scab control.
source: Naturally scab-suppressive soils have also been shown to contain a greater proportion of Pseudomonas when compared to scab-conducive soils (Meng et al., 2012; Rosenzweig et al., 2012), and phenazine production by P. fluorescens can contribute to scab control (Arseneault et al., 2015; Arseneault et al., 2013; Arseneault et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The P. fluorescens group consists of over 50 subspecies and exhibits huge phenotypic and genetic diversity.
source: Many soil pseudomonads belong to the Pseudomonas fluorescens group, which consists of over 50 subspecies and exhibits huge phenotypic and genetic diversity (Biessy et al., 2019; Gomila et al., 2015; Loper et al., 2012; Melnyk et al., 2019; Silby et al., 2009)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The P. fluorescens group has a core genome of about 1300 genes and a pan-genome of over 30,000 genes.
source: Many soil pseudomonads belong to the Pseudomonas fluorescens group, which consists of over 50 subspecies and exhibits huge phenotypic and genetic diversity (Biessy et al., 2019; Gomila et al., 2015; Loper et al., 2012; Melnyk et al., 2019; Silby et al., 2009), with a core genome of about 1300 genes and a pan-genome of over 30,000 genes (Garrido-Sanz et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Pseudomonas bacteria use a variety of mechanisms to colonize the plant rhizosphere.
